source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. X (Montreuil)

1.title: Elucidatio litteralis primi capituli: In anno secundo Darii regis.
1.title_en: Literal explanation of the first chapter: In the second year of Darius the king.

paras.t: Aggæus propheta, post reditum a Babylonica captivitate in Jerusalem, prophetavit ad eos qui de Babylonia redierunt, sicut ex littera mox exponenda ostenditur.
paras.en: Aggeus the prophet, after the return from the Babylonian captivity to Jerusalem, prophesied to those who had come back from Babylon, as is shown by the text that is now to be explained.

paras.t: Ait enim sanctus Propheta: In anno secundo regni Darii regis Persarum: qui secundum Hieronymum et Josephum, fuit filius Hystaspis; secundum alios vero, fuit filius Assueri regis et Esther reginæ. Unde Darius iste non fuit Darius ille, qui cum Cyro rege demolitus est Babylonem, sed longe posterior eo; imo posterior Cyro et Artaxerxe regibus Persarum. In mense sexto hujus anni secundi, in die una, id est prima, vel alia quadam die mensis istius, factum est verbum Domini in manu Aggæi prophetæ, id est ipsi Aggæo, atque in libero usu et actu ipsius. Per quod excluditur error dicentium, Prophetas esse locutos sicut loquuntur arrepticii et amentes: contra quos dicit Apostolus, Spiritus Prophetarum Prophetis subjecti sunt. Ad Zorobabel filium Salathiel: qui Salathiel natus est in Babylone, eratque filius Jechoniæ, juxta illud Matthæi: Et post transmigrationem Babylonis Jechonias genuit Salathiel. Ducem Juda. Erat namque Zorobabel de tribu Juda et semine David, ac principalis et dux inter Judæos secum de Chaldæa regressos. Et ad Jesum filium Josedec, sacerdotem magnum, id est inter sacerdotes temporis sui præcipuum, puta pontificem. Istis duobus tanquam capitibus populi, loquebatur Aggæus, deinde et aliis. Dicens:
paras.en: For the holy Prophet says: [[1:1|In the second year|In anno secundo]] of the reign [[1:1|of Darius the king|Darii regis]] of the Persians: who, according to Jerome and Josephus, was the son of Hystaspes, but according to others was the son of King Assuerus and Queen Esther. Hence this Darius was not that Darius who together with King Cyrus overthrew Babylon[[Dan 5:31||]], but came long after him; indeed, after Cyrus and Artaxerxes, kings of the Persians. [[1:1|in the sixth month|In mense sexto]] of this second year, [[1:1|in the first day|in die una]] [literally "on day one"], that is, the first, or some other day [[1:1|of the month|mensis]], [[1:1|the word of the Lord came by the hand of Haggai the prophet|factum est verbum Domini in manu Aggæi prophetæ]], that is, to Aggeus himself, and while he kept the free use and exercise of his own powers [Denis takes *in manu*, "by the hand", to mean that the prophet remained master of himself]. By this is excluded the error of those who say that the Prophets spoke as the possessed and the mad speak: against whom the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 14:32|the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets|Spiritus Prophetarum Prophetis subjecti sunt]]. [[1:1|to Zorobabel the son of Salathiel|Ad Zorobabel filium Salathiel]]: this Salathiel was born in Babylon and was the son of Jechonias, according to that word of Matthew: [[Matt 1:12|And after the transmigration of Babylon, Jechonias begot Salathiel|Et post transmigrationem Babylonis Jechonias genuit Salathiel]]. [[1:1|governor of Juda|Ducem Juda]] [*ducem*, "leader"]. For Zorobabel was of the tribe of Juda and of the seed of David, and the chief and leader among the Jews who had returned with him from Chaldea[[1 Esd 2:2||]]. [[1:1|and to Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest|Et ad Jesum filium Josedec, sacerdotem magnum]], that is, the foremost among the priests of his time, namely the pontiff. To these two, as to the heads of the people, Aggeus spoke, and then to the others also, [[1:1|saying|Dicens]]:

paras.t: Hæc ait Dominus exercituum, dicens: Populus iste de Babylone reversus, dicit, Nondum venit tempus domus Domini ædificandæ, id est, a constructione templi ignaviter se excusat. Porro, ut legitur secundo libro Paralipomenon et Esdræ primo libro, Cyrus rex Persarum concessit Judæis licentiam reparandi templum Dei in Jerusalem a Chaldæis destructum: sicque Judæi a Chaldæis reversi, cœperunt ædificare. Quumque altare construxissent, et fundamenta templi locassent, scripta est a Samaritanis epistola Artaxerxi regi contra eos, qui opus inceptum prohibuit exsequi. Itaque ex tunc impeditum fuit usque ad annum secundum Darii regis, ut legitur primo Esdræ libro. Quumque Darius iste dedisset Zorobabel licentiam consummandi templum inceptum, populus Judæorum adhuc tardus fuit ad prosequendum: ideo a Propheta redarguuntur, quemadmodum subditur.
paras.en: [[1:2|Thus saith the Lord of hosts, saying|Hæc ait Dominus exercituum, dicens]]: [[1:2|This people|Populus iste]], returned from Babylon, says, [[1:2|The time is not yet come for building the house of the Lord|Nondum venit tempus domus Domini ædificandæ]]; that is, they idly excuse themselves from building the temple. Now, as we read in the second book of Paralipomenon and the first book of Esdras, Cyrus king of the Persians granted the Jews leave to restore the temple of God in Jerusalem that the Chaldeans had destroyed[[2 Par 36:23||]][[1 Esd 1:2||]][[1 Esd 1:3||]][[1 Esd 1:4||]]; and so the Jews, returned from the Chaldeans, began to build. And when they had built the altar and laid the foundations of the temple[[1 Esd 3:1||]], a letter against them was written by the Samaritans to King Artaxerxes, and he forbade the work begun to be carried on[[1 Esd 4:1||]]. So from that time it was hindered until the second year of King Darius, as we read in the first book of Esdras[[1 Esd 6:1||]]. And when this Darius had given Zorobabel leave to finish the temple begun, the Jewish people were still slow to go on with it: therefore they are rebuked by the Prophet, as follows.

paras.t: Et factum est verbum Domini in manu Aggæi prophetæ, dicens. Secundum Hieronymum, revelatio ista prophetica eodem die est facta Aggæo, quo verbum præcedens.
paras.en: [[1:3|And the word of the Lord came by the hand of Haggai the prophet, saying|Et factum est verbum Domini in manu Aggæi prophetæ, dicens]]. According to Jerome, this prophetic revelation was made to Aggeus on the same day as the word before it.

paras.t: Numquid tempus vobis est, o Judæi, ut habetis in domibus laqueatis, id est ornatis et curiosis, et domus ista deserta, id est, templum adhuc permanet desolatum et irreparatum? Quasi dicat: Quamdiu domus Dei manet deserta, non decet ut vobis ipsis construatis ædificia amœna et pulchra.
paras.en: [[1:4|Is it time for you|Numquid tempus vobis est]], O Jews, [[1:4|to dwell in ceiled houses|ut habetis in domibus laqueatis]], that is, adorned and elaborate, [[1:4|and this house lie desolate|et domus ista deserta]], that is, the temple still remains desolate and unrepaired? As if to say: as long as the house of God remains deserted, it is not fitting that you should build pleasant and handsome dwellings for yourselves.

paras.t: Et nunc hæc dicit Dominus exercitum: Ponite corda vestra super vias vestras, id est, opera vestra sapienter pensate, et scietis quod male successerit vobis, eo quod operi Dei, videlicet templi ædificationi, prætuleritis proprium opus.
paras.en: [[1:5|And now thus saith the Lord of hosts|Et nunc hæc dicit Dominus exercitum]]: [[1:5|Set your hearts to consider your ways|Ponite corda vestra super vias vestras]]; that is, weigh your works wisely, and you will know that things have gone badly for you because you have put your own work before the work of God, namely the building of the temple.

paras.t: Nam Seminastis multum, et intulistis parum: ita quod seminationem paucus secutus est fructus, et terra quodammodo sterilis fuit. Comedistis, et non estis satiati; bibistis, et non estis inebriati, id est, sufficientiam cibi et potus non habuistis propter parvitatem fructuum terræ, segetum et uvarum. Itaque inebriatio non capitur hic, ut sonat vitiosam superfluitatem (sic enim non est pœna peccati, neque nocivum naturæ, non esse inebriatum), sed ut sufficientiam tantum vel exhilarationem quamdam cordis ex potu designat. Operuistis vos, et non estis calefacti: sicque indumentorum inopiam habuistis. Et qui mercedes, id est pecuniam vel alia quælibet, congregavit, ut thesaurizando vel negotiando lucraretur, misit eas in sacculum pertusum, id est, inutiliter eas amisit, sicut pecunia in sacculum confractum missa, elabitur atque deperditur. Hæc omnia contigerunt vobis propter acediam vestram circa templi instaurationem.
paras.en: For [[1:6|You have sowed much, and brought in little|Seminastis multum, et intulistis parum]]: so that little fruit followed the sowing, and the land was in a manner barren. [[1:6|you have eaten, but have not had enough|Comedistis, et non estis satiati]]; [[1:6|you have drunk, but have not been filled with drink|bibistis, et non estis inebriati]] [*inebriati*, literally "made drunk"]; that is, you have not had enough food and drink because of the meagreness of the fruits of the earth, of the crops and the grapes. So *inebriation* is not taken here in the sense of a vicious excess (for in that sense not being drunk is no punishment for sin, nor any harm to nature), but as it signifies only sufficiency, or a certain gladdening of the heart from drink. [[1:6|you have clothed yourselves, but have not been warmed|Operuistis vos, et non estis calefacti]]: and so you have lacked clothing. [[1:6|and he that hath earned wages|Et qui mercedes]] (that is, money or anything else), gathering them to make a profit by hoarding or by trading, [[1:6|put them into a bag with holes|misit eas in sacculum pertusum]]; that is, he lost them to no purpose, as money put into a broken bag slips out and is lost. All these things have befallen you because of your sloth [*acedia*, the sluggishness of spirit that shrinks from the things of God] over the restoration of the temple.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus exercitum: Ponite corda vestra super vias vestras. Ascendite in montem, id est ad loca silvestria et montana, in quibus sunt ligna pro templi ædificio apta, sicut in monte Libani; portate inde ligna. Vel: Ascendite in montem Sion, in quo construendum fuerat templum; portate ligna illuc. Et ædificate domum, videlicet templum; et acceptabilis mihi erit, et glorificabor, dicit Dominus, id est, gloriosus in ea apparebo, et mirabilia operabor, sicut infra patebit.
paras.en: [[1:7|Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Set your hearts upon your ways|Hæc dicit Dominus exercitum: Ponite corda vestra super vias vestras]]. [[1:8|Go up to the mountain|Ascendite in montem]], that is, to the wooded and mountainous places where there is timber fit for building the temple, as on Mount Libanus; [[1:8|bring|portate]] thence [[1:8|timber|ligna]]. Or: Go up to Mount Sion, on which the temple was to be built; bring timber there. [[1:8|and build the house|Et ædificate domum]], namely the temple; [[1:8|and it shall be acceptable to me, and I shall be glorified, saith the Lord|et acceptabilis mihi erit, et glorificabor, dicit Dominus]], that is, I will appear glorious in it and will work wonders, as will be seen below.

paras.t: Respexistis ad amplius, id est, multum de fructibus terræ habere putastis, et ecce factum est minus, id est, modicum et minus quam sperastis, fuit de ipsis bladis in culmis seu spicis. Et intulistis in domum, id est, in horrea terræ nascentia collegistis, et exsufflavi illud frumentum quod fuit in spicis, et mea virtute dispersum est, excidit, atque disperiit. Quam ob causam? dicit Dominus exercitum. Quia domus mea deserta est, id est, templum reparare neglexistis, et vos festinastis, alias festinatis, unusquisque in domum suam, id est, de proprio commodo et temporalibus bonis solliciti fuistis.
paras.en: [[1:9|You have looked for more|Respexistis ad amplius]], that is, you thought you would have much of the fruits of the earth, [[1:9|and behold it became less|et ecce factum est minus]]; that is, there was little, and less than you hoped, of the corn itself in the stalks or ears. [[1:9|and you brought it home|Et intulistis in domum]], that is, you gathered the produce of the earth into barns, [[1:9|and I blowed it away|et exsufflavi illud]], that is, that grain which was in the ears, and by my power it was scattered, fell away and perished. [[1:9|why, saith the Lord of hosts|Quam ob causam? dicit Dominus exercitum]]? [[1:9|because my house is desolate|Quia domus mea deserta est]], that is, you have neglected to repair the temple, [[1:9|and you make haste|et vos festinastis]] (another reading: *festinatis*) [[1:9|every man to his own house|unusquisque in domum suam]] [Denis's text reads *festinastis*, "you have made haste"; the other reading, *festinatis*, is that of the Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims]; that is, you have been anxious for your own convenience and for temporal goods.

paras.t: Propter hoc super vos prohibiti sunt cœli aerii ne darent rorem: id est, me ordinante atque jubente, nubes, rores et pluvia, in aere more solito generatæ non sunt, nec terram fecundaverunt; et terra prohibita est ne daret germen suum: quoniam ad prædictam siccitatem sterilitas est secuta. Terra quippe Juda de cœlo pluviam præstolatur, et inde fecundatur, quemadmodum in Deuteronomio Moyses loquitur: Terra ad quam ingredieris, non est sicut terra Ægypti, ubi jacto semine aquæ ducuntur irriguæ; sed montuosa est et campestris, de cœlo exspectans pluviam.
paras.en: [[1:10|Therefore the heavens over you were stayed from giving dew|Propter hoc super vos prohibiti sunt cœli aerii ne darent rorem]] [Denis reads *cœli aerii*, "the heavens of the air"]: that is, by my ordering and command, clouds, dews and rain were not formed in the air in the usual way, nor did they make the land fruitful; [[1:10|and the earth was hindered from yielding her fruits|et terra prohibita est ne daret germen suum]]: since barrenness followed upon the drought just mentioned. For the land of Juda waits for rain from heaven and is made fruitful by it, as Moses says in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 11:10|the land, which thou goest|Terra ad quam ingredieris]], [[Deut 11:10|is not like the land of Egypt|non est sicut terra Ægypti]], [[Deut 11:10|where, when the seed is sown, waters are brought in to water it|ubi jacto semine aquæ ducuntur irriguæ]]; [[Deut 11:11|But it is a land of hills and plains, expecting rain from heaven|sed montuosa est et campestris, de cœlo exspectans pluviam]].

paras.t: Et vocavi siccitatem super terram, et super montes, et super triticum, id est semen triticeum in terram projectum, vel super culmum exortum, ita quod fructus paucus secutus est; et super vinum et super oleum, id est super vites et uvas atque olivas, et quæcumque profert humus, id est super universa terræ nascentia; et super homines et super jumenta, id est ad vestram afflictionem et jumentorum famem ac sitim, quorum afflictio in vestræ redundavit calamitatis augmentum; et super omnem laborem manuum vestrarum, id est super possessiones vestras labore manuum acquisitas: ita quod siccitas illa aliquo modo nociva fuit omnibus quæ habetis, vel potius vobis per relationem ad illa.
paras.en: [[1:11|And I called for a drought upon the land, and upon the mountains, and upon the corn|Et vocavi siccitatem super terram, et super montes, et super triticum]], that is, the wheat seed cast into the ground, or upon the stalk that had sprung up, so that little fruit followed; [[1:11|and upon the wine, and upon the oil|et super vinum et super oleum]], that is, upon the vines and grapes and olives, [[1:11|and upon all that the ground bringeth forth|et quæcumque profert humus]], that is, upon all that springs from the earth; [[1:11|and upon men, and upon beasts|et super homines et super jumenta]], that is, to your affliction and to the hunger and thirst of the beasts, whose affliction went to increase your calamity; [[1:11|and upon all the labour of the hands|et super omnem laborem manuum vestrarum]] [Denis reads *manuum vestrarum*, "of your hands"], that is, upon your possessions gained by the labour of your hands: so that the drought was in some way harmful to everything you have, or rather to you, through your relation to those things.

paras.t: Et audivit Zorobabel filius Salathiel, et Jesus filius Josedec sacerdos magnus, et omnes reliquiæ populi, id est Judæi de captivitate reversi, et pauci de multis relicti, vocem Dei sui, et, pro id est, verba Aggæi prophetæ, id est, divinæ jussioni per Prophetam ad eos factæ obedierunt, sicut misit eum Dominus Deus eorum ad eos; et timuit omnis populus a facie Domini, id est, adspectum divinæ majestatis verebantur, et ex hoc processerunt in opus.
paras.en: [[1:12|Then Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest, and all the remnant of the people|Et audivit Zorobabel filius Salathiel, et Jesus filius Josedec sacerdos magnus, et omnes reliquiæ populi]], that is, the Jews returned from the captivity, the few left out of many, [[1:12|hearkened to the voice of the Lord their God|vocem Dei sui]] [Denis reads *vocem Dei sui*, "the voice of their God"], [[1:12|and|et]] (put here for *that is*) [[1:12|to the words of Haggai the prophet|verba Aggæi prophetæ]]; that is, they obeyed the divine command given to them through the Prophet, [[1:12|as the Lord their God sent him to them|sicut misit eum Dominus Deus eorum ad eos]]; [[1:12|and the people feared before the Lord|et timuit omnis populus a facie Domini]], that is, they stood in awe of the sight of the divine majesty, and from this they went forward to the work.

paras.t: Et dixit Aggæus nuntius Domini de nuntiis Domini, id est Propheta Dei de numero verorum Prophetarum exsistens, populo dicens: Ego vobiscum sum, dicit Dominus, id est, auxilium vobis præbebo, vosque tuebor, ita quod ædificatio vestra consummationem habebit. Vel sensus est, quod Aggæus nuntius Domini, dixit populo Judæorum præfato, de nuntiis Domini, id est de aliis Prophetis, vel ex parte seu persona eorum: Ego vobiscum sum, dicit Dominus. Quasi dicat: Non ego solus, sed alii quoque Prophetæ id ipsum testantur et spondent, dicentes quod dixi, videlicet, Ego vobiscum sum, dicit Dominus: quia per Jeremiam et Zachariam et Ezechielem Deus Judæis prædixit, quod post reditum de Babylone, adsisteret eis in omnibus.
paras.en: [[1:13|And Haggai the messenger of the Lord, as one of the messengers of the Lord|Et dixit Aggæus nuntius Domini de nuntiis Domini]], that is, a Prophet of God, being of the number of the true Prophets, [[1:13|spoke, saying to the people|populo dicens]]: [[1:13|I am with you, saith the Lord|Ego vobiscum sum, dicit Dominus]]; that is, I will give you help and will protect you, so that your building will be brought to completion. Or the sense is that Aggeus, [[1:13|the messenger of the Lord|nuntius Domini]], said to the Jewish people aforesaid, [[1:13|of the messengers of the Lord|de nuntiis Domini]] [Latin *de*, "of" or "from": in this second sense, "from the messengers"], that is, from the other Prophets, or on their part or in their person: [[1:13|I am with you, saith the Lord|Ego vobiscum sum, dicit Dominus]]. As if to say: not I alone, but the other Prophets too testify to this very thing and promise it, saying what I have said, namely, [[1:13|I am with you, saith the Lord|Ego vobiscum sum, dicit Dominus]]: for through Jeremias and Zacharias and Ezechiel God foretold to the Jews[[Jer 33:1||]][[Zach 8:1||]][[Ezech 34:1||]] that after the return from Babylon he would stand by them in all things.

paras.t: Et suscitavit Dominus spiritum Zorobabel filii Salathiel ducis Juda, et spiritum Jesu filii Josedec sacerdotis magni, et spiritum reliquorum de omni populo: id est, omnium horum animos inflammavit ac roboravit ad faciendum beneplacitum ejus; et ingressi sunt locum templi, et faciebant opus in domo Domini exercituum Dei sui: id est, ad templi constructionem quilibet, ut potuit, cooperabatur: non quod simpliciter omnes simul ingressi sint, sed quidam de omnibus, ut sit distributio accommoda, vel pro generibus singulorum. Ingressi sunt autem et ædificare exorsi sunt in die vicesima et quarta mensis, de quo in proœmio libri istius jam dictum est, utpote sexti mensis, sicut subjungitur, in sexto mense, in anno secundo Darii regis: ita quod inter primum diem hujus mensis, quo die ad Aggæum locutus est Dominus, et diem istum ejusdem mensis vicesimum quartum, fluxerunt mediique fuerunt dies viginti duo.
paras.en: [[1:14|And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zorobabel the son of Salathiel governor of Juda, and the spirit of Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest|Et suscitavit Dominus spiritum Zorobabel filii Salathiel ducis Juda, et spiritum Jesu filii Josedec sacerdotis magni]], [[1:14|and the spirit of all the rest of the people|et spiritum reliquorum de omni populo]]: that is, he kindled and strengthened the minds of all these to do his good pleasure; [[1:14|and they went in|et ingressi sunt]] to the place of the temple, [[1:14|and did the work in the house of the Lord of Hosts their God|et faciebant opus in domo Domini exercituum Dei sui]]: that is, each one, as he was able, worked together at the building of the temple: not that absolutely all went in together, but some of all, so that this is an accommodated distribution [a term of the logicians: *all* is taken for some of every kind, not for every single one], or one for the kinds of individuals [that is, for every sort of person, not for each person of every sort]. And they went in and began to build [[Agg 2:1|in the four and twentieth day of the month|in die vicesima et quarta mensis]] [in the Vulgate these words close chapter 1; the Douay-Rheims numbers them Aggeus 2:1], the month spoken of already in the prologue of this book, namely the sixth, as is added: [[Agg 2:1|in the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king|in sexto mense, in anno secundo Darii regis]]: so that between the first day of this month, the day on which the Lord spoke to Aggeus, and this twenty-fourth day of the same month, twenty-two days passed and lay in between.

1.title: De spirituali et mystico sensu ejusdem capituli primi.
1.title_en: On the spiritual and mystical sense of the same first chapter.

paras.t: Aggæus interpretatur solennitas. Qui ergo a peccatis sæculique tumultibus et passionum strepitibus cessat, et in mentis quiete sabbatum delicatum Domino celebrat, solis divinis contemplando ac diligendo intendens, capax est revelationum cœlestium, et dignus aptusque ut verbum Dei fiat ad ipsum, ita quod unctio Spiritus Sancti docet eum de omnibus. Denique per hujusmodi virum loquitur Deus ad Zorobabel, qui interpretatur magister in Babylone, hoc est ad principes sæculares, qui temporali præsunt regimini, in quo variæ confusiones vitiorum occurrunt. Babylonis autem nomine, mundus exprimitur. Et ad Jesum sacerdotem magnum, id est ad prælatos Ecclesiæ, qui aliorum salutem procurare, quantum in ipsis est, debent. Jesus autem salus vel salutaris interpretatur.
paras.en: Aggeus is interpreted *solemnity* [that is, a feast: the name comes from the Hebrew word for a festival]. He, then, who ceases from sins, from the tumults of the world and the clamour of the passions, and in quiet of mind keeps a delightful sabbath to the Lord [the phrase "delightful sabbath" is from Isaias 58:13], intent on divine things alone, contemplating and loving them, is capable of heavenly revelations, and worthy and fit that the word of God should come to him, so that the unction of the Holy Ghost teaches him of all things[[1 John 2:27||]]. Through such a man, then, God speaks [[1:1|to Zorobabel|ad Zorobabel]], which is interpreted *master in Babylon*: that is, to secular princes, who preside over temporal government, in which various confusions of vices are met with; for by the name of Babylon the world is expressed. [[1:1|and to Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest|Et ad Jesum sacerdotem magnum]], that is, to the prelates of the Church, who ought to procure the salvation of others as far as in them lies. Now *Jesus* is interpreted *salvation* or *saving*.

paras.t: Porro, secundum Hieronymum, uterque istorum, Christi fuit figura. Christus enim rex et dux noster est : sicque Zorobabel typus fuit ipsius. Ipse quoque magnus et summus sacerdos est, juxta illud in Psalmo, Tu es sacerdos in æternum : de quo scriptum est in prima Canonica Petri, Conversi estis ad pastorem et episcopum animarum vestrarum : sicque per Jesum filium Josedec figurabatur. Quemadmodum enim isti populum suum de Babylone in terram promissionis reduxerunt; sic Christus Jesus suos electos de diabolica captivitate sæcularisque vitæ confusione eripuit, et de mundo isto confusionibus pleno, ad regionem cœlestem evexit, juxta illud ad Hebræos, Multos filios adduxit in gloriam.
paras.en: Further, according to Jerome, each of these two was a figure of Christ. For Christ is our king and leader [*dux*, the word rendered "governor" in v. 1, where Zorobabel is *dux Juda*], and so Zorobabel was a type of him. He is also the great and high priest, according to that in the Psalm, [[Ps 109:4|Thou art a priest for ever|Tu es sacerdos in æternum]]; of whom it is written in the first canonical Epistle of Peter, [[1 Pet 2:25|you are now converted to the shepherd and bishop of your souls|Conversi estis ad pastorem et episcopum animarum vestrarum]]; and so he was figured by Jesus the son of Josedec. For as these two led their people back from Babylon into the land of promise, so Christ Jesus has snatched his elect from the captivity of the devil and from the confusion of worldly life, and from this world full of confusions has carried them up to the heavenly country, according to that to the Hebrews: [[Heb 2:10|who had brought many children into glory|Multos filios adduxit in gloriam]].

paras.t: Insuper, quid Dominus per spiritualem Aggæum ad principes sæculares fideles, ecclesiasticosque prælatos dicat, advertentia dignum est. Hæc ait Dominus : Populus iste dicit, Nondum venit tempus domus Domini ædificandæ : id est, plebs vobis subdita et commissa, verbis vel rebus affirmat, nondum adesse horam reformandi Ecclesiam, corrigendi mores, emendandi vitam. Domus equidem Dei, est congregatio fidelium, vel unusquisque devotus, seu anima justi. Deus namque habitat in cordibus nostris per fidem, et corpora nostra templum sunt Spiritus Sancti, secundum Apostolum. Qui ergo se ipsum vel proximum noscit gratiam Dei amisisse, et domum diaboli factum peccando : si iste emendationem sui vel proximi protrahit, differt, procrastinat, nec statim pœnitentiam agit condignam; etsi non verbis, tamen rebus asserit : Nondum venit tempus domus Dei ædificandæ. Præcipue quoque circa hoc damnabiles approbabuntur principes et prælati, qui gregem sibi commissum verbo et opere ædificare non satagunt, sed malum paulatim increscere sinunt. Quibus Salomon ait : Usquequo, piger, dormies? Quibus et in Isaia Dominus loquitur : Speculatores cæci, etc., canes muti, non valentes latrare, videntes vana, et dormientes.
paras.en: Moreover, it is worth attending to what the Lord says through the spiritual Aggeus to faithful secular princes and to the prelates of the Church. [[1:2|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc ait Dominus]]: [[1:2|This people saith: The time is not yet come for building the house of the Lord|Populus iste dicit, Nondum venit tempus domus Domini ædificandæ]]: that is, the people subject and committed to you affirm, by words or by deeds, that the hour has not yet come for reforming the Church, correcting morals, amending life. Now the house of God is the congregation of the faithful, or each devout person, or the soul of the just. For God dwells in our hearts by faith[[Eph 3:17||]], and our bodies are [[1 Cor 6:19|the temple of the Holy Ghost|templum sunt Spiritus Sancti]], according to the Apostle. Whoever, then, knows that he himself or his neighbour has lost the grace of God and by sinning has become a house of the devil: if he draws out, defers and puts off the amendment of himself or of his neighbour, and does not at once do worthy penance, then, though not in words, yet in deeds he declares: [[1:2|The time is not yet come for building the house of the Lord|Nondum venit tempus domus Dei ædificandæ]]. Princes and prelates especially will be proved damnable in this respect, who do not take pains to build up by word and work the flock committed to them, but let evil grow little by little. To them Solomon says: [[Prov 6:9|How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard?|Usquequo, piger, dormies?]] To them also the Lord speaks in Isaias: [[Is 56:10|His watchmen are all blind|Speculatores cæci]], etc., [[Is 56:10|dumb dogs not able to bark, seeing vain things, sleeping|canes muti, non valentes latrare, videntes vana, et dormientes]].

paras.t: Præterea universis carnalibus, temporalia et terrena magis quam cœlestia et æterna quærentibus, magisque hominibus quam Deo placere optantibus, rectissime dicitur : Hæc dicit Dominus : Numquid tempus vobis est ut habitetis in domibus laqueatis, id est corporibus vestris curiose atque pompose ornatis, et domus ista deserta, id est, ipsa vestra conscientia, mens seu anima, quæ Dei domus esse deberet, a vobis negligitur et gratia spoliatur, spiritualiterque destruitur? Sicut enim docet Apostolus, virtuosi habitant et sunt in spiritu, vitiosi autem in carne. Itaque qui corporibus suis de omnibus commodis carneis diligenter abundanterque provident, animam vero virtutibus vacuam, a caritate frigentem, vitiis sauciam, non reformant nec ornant : isti divinitus increpantur, carnales vocantur, et omni damnatione digni censentur.
paras.en: Furthermore, to all carnal men, who seek temporal and earthly things more than heavenly and eternal ones, and wish to please men rather than God, it is most rightly said: Thus saith the Lord: [[1:4|Is it time for you to dwell in ceiled houses|Numquid tempus vobis est ut habitetis in domibus laqueatis]], that is, in your bodies curiously and pompously adorned, [[1:4|and this house lie desolate|et domus ista deserta]], that is, while your very conscience, mind or soul, which ought to be the house of God, is neglected by you, stripped of grace and spiritually destroyed? For, as the Apostle teaches, the virtuous dwell and are in the spirit, but the vicious in the flesh[[Rom 8:8||]][[Rom 8:9||]]. And so those who diligently and abundantly provide their bodies with every fleshly comfort, but do not reform or adorn the soul, empty of virtues, cold in charity, wounded by vices: these are rebuked by God, are called carnal, and are judged worthy of all damnation.

paras.t: Præterea præinductis utique verbis redarguuntur carnales Christiani, qui Dei zelo non fervent, sed privato pleni amore sunt, ideoque materialia Christi templa, et domus divino cultui deputatas, inveterata, ruinosa, et quotidie deficientia vel destructa reparare, ædificare, constabilire non enituntur, sed sibimetipsis habitacula construunt curiosa, voluptuosa, superflua. In istis amor Christi non viget : quibus Isaias minatur, Væ qui conjungitis domum ad domum, et agrum, etc., et opus Dei non respicitis.
paras.en: Furthermore, the words quoted above certainly reprove carnal Christians who do not burn with zeal for God but are full of private love, and therefore do not strive to repair, build up and make firm the material temples of Christ and the houses set apart for divine worship, when they are old, ruinous, and every day falling into decay or destroyed, but build for themselves dwellings that are elaborate, luxurious and superfluous. In these the love of Christ is not strong; and Isaias threatens them: [[Is 5:8|Woe to you that join house to house and lay field|Væ qui conjungitis domum ad domum, et agrum]], etc., [[Is 5:12|and the work of the Lord you regard not|et opus Dei non respicitis]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus : Ponite corda vestra, id est mentis vestræ considerationem, super vias vestras, id est affectiones, cogitatus et opera, ut sitis in omnibus circumspecti : quemadmodum ait Apostolus ad Timotheum, Sine præjudicio, id est prævio rationis judicio, nihil facias; Salomon quoque, Oculi tui videant recta, et palpebræ tuæ præcedant gressus tuos. Hoc est quod in Ecclesiastico legitur : Fili, sine consilio nihil facias, et post factum non pœnitebis. Hoc modo posuit sanctus Job cor suum super vias suas, qui dixit : Verebar omnia opera mea, sciens quod non parceres, Domine, delinquenti. Quum enim, secundum positionem probabilem, in actibus humanis non sit indifferens, id est aliquid quod nec meritorium nec demeritorium sit : qui modo præfato corda sua super vias suas non ponunt, nonne quotidie quasi innumerabilia peccata incurrunt, cogitando, loquendo, appetendo et operando, imo et debita omittendo? Tales sunt omnes intimorati, qui implere non curant quod scriptum est : Omni custodia custodi cor tuum.
paras.en: [[1:7|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[1:7|Set your hearts|Ponite corda vestra]], that is, the consideration of your mind, [[1:7|upon your ways|super vias vestras]], that is, your affections, thoughts and works, so that you may be circumspect in all things: as the Apostle says to Timothy, [[1 Tim 5:21|without prejudice|Sine præjudicio]], that is, without a judgement of reason going before, do nothing [Denis takes *præjudicium* as "a judgement made beforehand": do nothing without first weighing it by reason]; and Solomon too: [[Prov 4:25|Let thy eyes look straight on, and let thy eyelids go before thy steps|Oculi tui videant recta, et palpebræ tuæ præcedant gressus tuos]]. This is what we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 32:24|My son, do thou nothing without counsel, and thou shalt not repent when thou hast done|Fili, sine consilio nihil facias, et post factum non pœnitebis]]. In this way holy Job set his heart upon his ways, who said: [[Job 9:28|I feared all my works, knowing that thou didst not spare|Verebar omnia opera mea, sciens quod non parceres]], O Lord, [[Job 9:28|the offender|delinquenti]]. For since, according to a probable opinion, there is nothing indifferent in human acts [that is, no deliberate human act, taken as actually done, is morally neutral], that is, nothing that is neither meritorious nor demeritorious: do not those who fail to set their hearts upon their ways in the manner described fall every day into sins almost without number, by thinking, speaking, desiring and acting, and indeed by leaving undone what they ought to do? Such are all the unfearing [*intimorati*, those without the fear of God], who do not trouble to fulfil what is written: [[Prov 4:23|With all watchfulness keep thy heart|Omni custodia custodi cor tuum]].

paras.t: Ascendite in montem, id est ad Christum, ejus documenta atque exempla pensando et imitando, vel ad spiritualem et altam sacræ Scripturæ intelligentiam, vel ad veram mentis perfectionem. Portate ligna, id est, dona Sancti Spiritus obtinere conemini. Unde de sapientia quæ est primum inter dona, Salomon profitetur : Lignum vitæ est omnibus apprehendentibus eam. His quippe donis tanquam fortissimis lignis machina virtutum consurgit et stabilitur in anima. Et ædificate domum conscientiæ, aliosque in virtutibus reformate; et acceptabilis mihi erit spiritualis hæc domus : et deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum; et glorificabor in ea, dicit Dominus, id est, a fidelibus honorabor, gloriosus agnoscar, et majestatis ac gratiæ meæ potentiam ipsis monstrabo.
paras.en: [[1:8|Go up to the mountain|Ascendite in montem]], that is, to Christ, by weighing and imitating his teachings and examples; or to the spiritual and lofty understanding of Holy Scripture; or to true perfection of mind. [[1:8|bring timber|Portate ligna]], that is, strive to obtain the gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]]. Hence Solomon declares of wisdom, which is the first among the gifts: [[Prov 3:18|She is a tree of life to them that lay hold on her|Lignum vitæ est omnibus apprehendentibus eam]] [*ligna*, "timber", and *lignum*, "tree", are the same word in Latin]. For by these gifts, as by the strongest timbers, the structure of the virtues rises and is made firm in the soul. [[1:8|and build the house|Et ædificate domum]] of conscience, and reform others in the virtues; [[1:8|and it shall be acceptable to me|et acceptabilis mihi erit]], this spiritual house: and [[Prov 8:31|my delights were to be with the children of men|deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum]]; [[1:8|and I shall be glorified|et glorificabor]] in it, [[1:8|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]]: that is, I shall be honoured by the faithful, acknowledged as glorious, and shall show them the power of my majesty and grace.

paras.t: Respexistis ad amplius, id est, grandem in virtutibus perfectionem obtinere putastis, et factum est minus, id est, parum vel nihil profecistis. Et intulistis in domum, id est, aliquid gratiæ impetrastis, et mentis areæ induxistis, et exsufflavi illud, id est, perire permisi, nec mea custodia dignum putavi. Hoc illis contingit qui divino honori commoda sua præponunt, et privatum atque carnalem amorem funditus non exstirpant : quorum pœnitentia et devotio instabiles ostenduntur, quia dum tentatio parva occurrit, mox superantur. Tales sunt audaces, sibi placentes, sapientes et magni in oculis suis, qui conversationem suam in vera ac stabili humilitate non fundant.
paras.en: [[1:9|You have looked for more|Respexistis ad amplius]], that is, you thought to obtain great perfection in the virtues, [[1:9|and behold it became less|et factum est minus]], that is, you made little or no progress. [[1:9|and you brought it home|Et intulistis in domum]], that is, you obtained some grace and brought it into the threshing floor of the mind, [[1:9|and I blowed it away|et exsufflavi illud]], that is, I let it perish, and did not think it worthy of my keeping. This happens to those who put their own advantage before the honour of God and do not root out private and carnal love completely: their penance and devotion prove unstable, for as soon as a small temptation comes they are overcome. Such are the [[2 Pet 2:10|audacious, self willed|audaces, sibi placentes]], wise and great in their own eyes[[Is 5:21||]], who do not ground their way of life in true and stable humility.

paras.t: Seminastis multum, et intulistis parum. Hoc accidit illis qui in exterioribus observantiis corporalibusque exercitationibus multum se occupant, et circa interiorem animæ reformationem atque internam in Deo caritatis affectionem parum proficiunt. Propter quod dicit Apostolus : Corporalis exercitatio ad modicum utilis est; pietas autem ad omnia valet.
paras.en: [[1:6|You have sowed much, and brought in little|Seminastis multum, et intulistis parum]]. This happens to those who busy themselves much with outward observances and bodily exercises, and make little progress in the inward reform of the soul and the inner affection of charity towards God. For which reason the Apostle says: [[1 Tim 4:8|bodily exercise is profitable to little: but godliness is profitable to all things|Corporalis exercitatio ad modicum utilis est; pietas autem ad omnia valet]].

paras.t: Comedistis, et non estis satiati ; bibistis, et non estis inebriati. Hoc de his accipi potest qui corpus et sanguinem Christi vel indigne, vel minus digne suscipiunt, quoniam sacramenti virtutem et efficaciam non sortiuntur propter vitæ suæ negligentiam et torporem ; item de his qui aqua sapientiæ et pane vitæ operibusque virtutum, et pane potuque lacrimarum vescuntur, aliquidque spiritualis consolationis experiuntur, sed non satis condigne secundum vocationis suæ exigentiam crescunt in istis : quibus advertendum est illud apostoli Pauli, Resuscites gratiam Dei in te; et rursus : Digne ambuletis vocatione qua vocati estis; illud quoque Joannis, Memor esto unde excideris.
paras.en: [[1:6|you have eaten, but have not had enough: you have drunk, but have not been filled with drink|Comedistis, et non estis satiati ; bibistis, et non estis inebriati]]. This can be taken of those who receive the body and blood of Christ either unworthily or not worthily enough, since they do not obtain the power and effect of the sacrament because of the negligence and torpor of their lives; and also of those who feed on the water of wisdom and the bread of life[[Ecclus 15:3||]] and on the works of the virtues, and on the bread and drink of tears[[Ps 79:6||]], and taste something of spiritual consolation, but do not grow in these things worthily enough, as their calling requires. These should heed that saying of the apostle Paul, [[2 Tim 1:6|stir up the grace of God which is in thee|Resuscites gratiam Dei in te]]; and again: [[Eph 4:1|walk worthy of the vocation in which you are called|Digne ambuletis vocatione qua vocati estis]]; and that of John too, [[Apoc 2:5|Be mindful therefore from whence thou art fallen|Memor esto unde excideris]].

paras.t: Operuistis vos pallio caritatis et indumentis justitiæ, et non estis calefacti fervore divini amoris. Hoc dicitur his qui quum spiritu cœperint, carne consummantur, qui a pristino cadunt fervore, atque in via Dei regrediuntur magis quam progrediantur. Et qui mercedes congregavit, id est, bene agendo aliqua sibi merita et præmia accumulavit, misit eas in sacculum pertusum, id est, fructum laborum suorum amisit, non perseverando usque in finem, vel laudes humanas quærendo, vel intra se inaniter gloriando, nec intra humilitatis custodiam spirituales divitias conservando. Tales sunt vani atque inutiles homines : de quibus ait Salvator, Amen dico vobis, receperunt mercedem suam. Thesaurizemus ergo in cœlo, omneque bonum Deo humiliter adscribamus.
paras.en: [[1:6|you have clothed yourselves|Operuistis vos]] with the mantle of charity and the garments of justice, [[1:6|but have not been warmed|et non estis calefacti]] with the fervour of divine love. This is said to those who, having begun in the spirit, end in the flesh[[Gal 3:3||]]; who fall from their first fervour, and go backward in the way of God rather than forward. [[1:6|and he that hath earned wages|Et qui mercedes congregavit]], that is, has heaped up for himself some merits and rewards by doing good, [[1:6|put them into a bag with holes|misit eas in sacculum pertusum]], that is, has lost the fruit of his labours, by not persevering to the end, or by seeking human praise, or by glorying vainly within himself, and by not keeping his spiritual riches within the guard of humility. Such are vain and useless men, of whom the Saviour says: [[Matt 6:2|Amen I say to you, they have received their reward|Amen dico vobis, receperunt mercedem suam]][[Matt 6:5||]][[Matt 6:16||]]. Let us therefore lay up treasure in heaven[[Matt 6:20||]], and humbly ascribe every good thing to God[[Jas 1:17||]].

paras.t: Quam ob causam? dicit Dominus. Quia domus mea deserta est, id est, thalamus conscientiæ non purgatus, proximus ad pœnitentiam non conversus, et plebs a dæmonum jugo non revocata; et vos festinastis unusquisque in domum suam, propria commoda exquirendo, atque in carnis vitiis persistendo.
paras.en: [[1:9|why, saith the Lord|Quam ob causam? dicit Dominus]]? [[1:9|because my house is desolate|Quia domus mea deserta est]], that is, the bridal chamber of the conscience is not cleansed, the neighbour is not converted to penance, and the people are not called back from the yoke of the demons; [[1:9|and you make haste every man to his own house|et vos festinastis unusquisque in domum suam]], by seeking your own advantage and persisting in the vices of the flesh.

paras.t: Propter hoc super vos prohibiti sunt cœli, id est spiritus angelici, ne darent rorem, id est, ne corda vestra gratiæ influentia instrumentaliter fecundarent, consolationemque cœlestis dulcedinis ad vos deferrent. Vel cœli isti, sunt viri devoti et prædicatores verbi Dei, in terra cœliformiter conversantes : a quibus Deus sæpe subtrahit efficaciam exhortandi propter negligentiam populi, quemadmodum ad Ezechielem loquitur Deus : Fili hominis, linguam tuam adhærere faciam palato tuo, et eris mutus, nec quasi vir objurgans, quia domus exasperans est. De hoc rore loquitur Isaias ad Dominum : Ros tuus ros lucis ; Isaac quoque ad Jacob, Det tibi Deus de rore cœli. Et terra continuit germen suum, id est, habitantes in terra, fructum virtutum non protulerunt. Non enim sine gratiæ influxu aliquid meritorie agere queunt. Ideo profitetur Psalmista : Expandi manus meas ad te ; anima mea sicut terra sine aqua tibi.
paras.en: [[1:10|Therefore the heavens over you were stayed|Propter hoc super vos prohibiti sunt cœli]], that is, the angelic spirits, [[1:10|from giving dew|ne darent rorem]], that is, from making your hearts fruitful, as instruments, by the inflowing of grace, and from bringing you the consolation of heavenly sweetness. Or these heavens are devout men and preachers of the word of God, living a heavenly life on earth: from them God often withdraws the power to exhort because of the negligence of the people, as God speaks to Ezechiel: [[Ezech 3:25|O son of man|Fili hominis]], [[Ezech 3:26|I will make thy tongue stick fast to the roof of thy mouth, and thou shalt be dumb, and not as a man that reproveth: because they are a provoking house|linguam tuam adhærere faciam palato tuo, et eris mutus, nec quasi vir objurgans, quia domus exasperans est]]. Of this dew Isaias speaks to the Lord: [[Is 26:19|thy dew is the dew of the light|Ros tuus ros lucis]]; and Isaac to Jacob: [[Gen 27:28|God give thee of the dew of heaven|Det tibi Deus de rore cœli]]. [[1:10|and the earth was hindered from yielding her fruits|Et terra continuit germen suum]] [Denis reads *terra continuit germen suum*, "the earth held back its fruit"], that is, those who dwell on the earth have not brought forth the fruit of the virtues. For without the inflowing of grace they cannot do anything meritorious. Hence the Psalmist declares: [[Ps 142:6|I stretched forth my hands to thee: my soul is as earth without water unto thee|Expandi manus meas ad te ; anima mea sicut terra sine aqua tibi]].

paras.t: Et vocavi siccitatem super terram, id est, virtuosorum operum sterilitatem sive carentiam super eos qui dediti sunt peccatis carnalibus. Unde homini in vitium gulæ prolapso, dictum est a Deo : Terra es, et in terram ibis. Sed et in Genesi protestatus est Dominus : Non permanebit spiritus meus in homine in æternum, quia caro est. Et super montes, id est eos qui spiritualibus vitiis, præsertim superbiæ, serviunt. Deus quippe superbis resistit. Et super triticum, et super vinum et oleum, et quæcumque profert humus, id est super universa quæ agunt, quia etsi quid de genere bonorum agere videantur, Deo tamen absolute non placet, nec quidpiam promerentur, eo quod caritatem Dei infusam sortiti non sint. Et super homines et jumenta, id est doctos in sua scientia tumidos, et indoctos, vel super credentes fide informi atque incredulos.
paras.en: [[1:11|And I called for a drought upon the land|Et vocavi siccitatem super terram]], that is, barrenness or want of virtuous works upon those who are given to carnal sins. Hence to man, when he had fallen into the vice of gluttony, God said: [[Gen 3:19|dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return|Terra es, et in terram ibis]] [Denis reads *terra*, "earth", for *pulvis*, "dust": the same word as the "land" of this verse]. And in Genesis the Lord also declared: [[Gen 6:3|My spirit shall not remain in man for ever, because he is flesh|Non permanebit spiritus meus in homine in æternum, quia caro est]]. [[1:11|and upon the mountains|Et super montes]], that is, upon those who serve spiritual vices, above all pride. For [[Jas 4:6|God resisteth the proud|Deus quippe superbis resistit]][[1 Pet 5:5||]]. [[1:11|and upon the corn, and upon the wine, and upon the oil, and upon all that the ground bringeth forth|Et super triticum, et super vinum et oleum, et quæcumque profert humus]], that is, upon all that they do: for even if they seem to do something of the kind that is good, it still does not please God absolutely, nor do they merit anything, because they have not received the infused charity of God. [[1:11|and upon men, and upon beasts|Et super homines et jumenta]], that is, upon the learned puffed up with their knowledge, and upon the unlearned; or upon those who believe with unformed faith [that is, faith without charity], and upon unbelievers.

paras.t: Et audivit Zorobabel, et Jesus filius Josedec, et reliquiæ populi vocem Dei et verba Aggæi prophetæ. Electi enim et timorati ac dociles, divinis eloquiis et devotorum exhortationibus acquiescunt. Et timuit populus a facie Domini. Vultus enim Domini super facientes mala, ut perdat de terra memoriam eorum : et certe divinæ majestatis præsentia cum ingenti reverentia est timenda.
paras.en: [[1:12|Then Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest, and all the remnant of the people hearkened to the voice of the Lord their God, and to the words of Haggai the prophet|Et audivit Zorobabel, et Jesus filius Josedec, et reliquiæ populi vocem Dei et verba Aggæi prophetæ]]. For the elect, the God-fearing and the teachable, assent to the divine words and to the exhortations of the devout. [[1:12|and the people feared before the Lord|Et timuit populus a facie Domini]]. For [[Ps 33:17|the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth|Vultus enim Domini super facientes mala, ut perdat de terra memoriam eorum]]: and certainly the presence of the divine majesty is to be feared with great reverence.

paras.t: Et suscitavit Dominus spiritum Zorobabel, et spiritum Jesu filii Josedec, et spiritum reliquorum de populo ; et ingressi, faciebant opus in domo Domini. Simili modo dum Spiritus Sanctus excitat corda prælatorum ac principum et subditorum, ingrediuntur ecclesiam propriamque conscientiam, et divina exsequuntur mandata.
paras.en: [[1:14|And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zorobabel the son of Salathiel governor of Juda, and the spirit of Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest, and the spirit of all the rest of the people: and they went in, and did the work in the house of the Lord|Et suscitavit Dominus spiritum Zorobabel, et spiritum Jesu filii Josedec, et spiritum reliquorum de populo ; et ingressi, faciebant opus in domo Domini]]. In like manner, when the Holy Ghost stirs up the hearts of prelates and princes and subjects, they enter the church and their own conscience, and carry out the divine commandments.
